articles.title: Wolfspeed Secures Conditional $1.5 Billion U.S. Department Of War Loan Commitment
articles.snippet:
Wolfspeed received a conditional commitment from the U.S. Department of War for up to $1.5 billion in long-term financing to support domestic production of silicon carbide materials and wide bandgap power devices, with an additional focus on U.S. national security applications.
The post Wolfspeed Secures Conditional $1.5 Billion U.S. Department Of War Loan Commitment appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Wolfspeed Secures Conditional $1.5 Billion U.S. Department Of War Loan Commitment
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 13, 2026
Wolfspeed Secures Conditional $1.5 Billion U.S. Department Of War Loan Commitment
Wolfspeed received a conditional commitment from the U.S. Department of War for up to $1.5 billion in long-term financing to support domestic production of silicon carbide materials and wide bandgap power devices, with an additional focus on U.S. national security applications.
The financing would be provided through the Department of War’s Office of Strategic Capital and is structured as a senior secured delayed-draw term loan facility with a 30-year tenor.
Wolfspeed plans to use the potential financing to strengthen its U.S. semiconductor manufacturing capabilities across silicon carbide and gallium nitride technologies.
The company said the financing could support upgrades to its gallium nitride epitaxy capabilities for next-generation communications infrastructure and electronic warfare systems.
It also plans to develop radiation-hardening capabilities for existing silicon carbide products and future gallium nitride products.
Wolfspeed said silicon carbide and related semiconductor technologies are increasingly important across defense, aerospace, artificial intelligence, critical infrastructure, and other strategic commercial markets.
The company’s domestic manufacturing footprint includes operations in North Carolina, New York, and Arkansas.
The financing is expected to support a multi-year program to strengthen Wolfspeed’s leadership in U.S. silicon carbide materials and power devices.
Wolfspeed also plans to establish, expand, or onshore domestic low-voltage and high-voltage gallium nitride power-device production capabilities.
Additional priorities include advancing GaN-on-SiC radio-frequency epitaxial wafer technology and developing domestic radiation-hardening capabilities.
The company said the financing would also strengthen its capital structure and provide additional long-duration funding for strategic investments.
Under the contemplated structure, Wolfspeed would be required to issue warrants to the Department of War representing up to 7.5% of the company’s fully diluted equity.
Those warrants would be issued on a pro rata basis as financing tranches are funded.
The transaction remains subject to substantial due diligence, negotiation and execution of definitive agreements, governmental approvals, appropriations, third-party consents, and other closing conditions.
Wolfspeed said there is no assurance that definitive agreements will be completed or that the financing will ultimately be funded.
The conditional commitment represents another step in Wolfspeed’s broader effort to strengthen its financial foundation while expanding its role in the domestic wide bandgap semiconductor supply chain.

Robert Feurle, Chief Executive Officer of Wolfspeed
“We believe the scale and 30-year tenor of this conditional commitment reflects the long-term importance of the technology and manufacturing capabilities Wolfspeed has built in the United States. Eka Robotics Hits $1.45 Billion Valuation After $150 Million Funding Round for Physical AI
Eka Robotics raises $150 million at a $1.45 billion valuation to advance physical AI, touch-sensitive robotic grippers and industrial automation.
By
Samarjit Kaur
on
October 21, 2026
Share
Eka Robotics is developing physical AI technology that combines force-sensitive robotic grippers with machine learning to improve object handling.
Eka Robotics, a startup developing artificial intelligence (AI) systems for robots, has secured a $1.45 billion post-money valuation after raising $150 million in Series A funding. Founded by Massachusetts Institute of Technology professor Pulkit Agrawal and former Google DeepMind researcher Tuomas Haarnoja, the company is developing technology that lets robots pick up and handle objects faster and more precisely.
The funding round was led by venture capital firms Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) & F-Prime.
The startup’s approach combines a force-sensitive robotic gripper with a deep-learning model trained to respond to physical contact, addressing a longstanding challenge in robotics.
Also Read: Indian Startup Unveils Vision Nano 250g UAV for Special Forces, Claims 25-Minute Flight Time
How Eka Robotics is Changing Robotic Manipulation
Eka Robotics says its system can pick up about 1,500 objects weighing up to 1 kg per hour, compared with about 600 for a human. The company also reports a success rate of more than 95% when picking up objects.
Unlike conventional approaches that rely heavily on visual information, Eka uses what it calls a vision-force-action model. The system combines visual & language inputs with physical-force information, helping the robot adjust its grip when handling delicate objects.
Its robotic hand includes additional force sensors and a more flexible design than traditional grippers. This allows it to respond to contact rather than relying on sight alone.
The founders use physics simulations and reinforcement learning to train the system. This approach can generate thousands of hours of robotic experience in minutes, reducing reliance on lengthy recordings of humans demonstrating tasks.
University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign professor Kris Hauser told TechCrunch that the robot could adapt to numerous objects without retraining. However, the technology’s performance in industrial settings remains to be established.
Also Read: AI Startup Demoverse Raises $600K to Let Consumers Co-Create Products With Brands
Industrial Deployment Remains the Next Test
Eka Robotics is running confidential pilot projects with industrial customers that involve pick-and-place operations and wire manipulation. These tasks involve moving objects into position and handling wires during assembly.
The company faces the actionable challenge of proving that its systems can operate reliably on production lines for extended periods. Hauser also questioned how readily the approach could be adapted to industrial tasks beyond basic object handling.
Agrawal said the company’s gripper hardware costs less than $1,000 and is currently rated for five million duty cycles. The longer-term target is 20 million cycles, matching the benchmark cited for standard industrial robotic arms.

articles.title: Clean Power Alliance Secures $1.4 Billion Prepay Bond To Generate $91.1 Million In Renewable Energy Savings
articles.snippet:
Clean Power Alliance has closed its seventh energy prepayment bond transaction, a $1.4 billion financing expected to generate approximately $91.1 million in renewable energy cost savings during the bond’s initial seven-year period.
The post Clean Power Alliance Secures $1.4 Billion Prepay Bond To Generate $91.1 Million In Renewable Energy Savings appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Clean Power Alliance Secures $1.4 Billion Prepay Bond To Generate $91.1 Million In Renewable Energy Savings
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 19, 2026
Clean Power Alliance Secures $1.4 Billion Prepay Bond To Generate $91.1 Million In Renewable Energy Savings
Clean Power Alliance has closed its seventh energy prepayment bond transaction, a $1.4 billion financing expected to generate approximately $91.1 million in renewable energy cost savings during the bond’s initial seven-year period.
The transaction is projected to deliver average savings of approximately $12.7 million annually. With the latest issuance, Clean Power Alliance has now completed $8.3 billion in prepay bond transactions and locked in $519.1 million in total savings across the initial periods of the seven transactions.
Across the entire program, CPA said its average annual savings total approximately $65 million.
The organization uses its prepay bond program to lower the cost of renewable power purchases. As a not-for-profit government agency, CPA can issue tax-exempt bonds and use the proceeds to prepay for electricity generated from renewable resources such as solar, wind, geothermal, and hydropower. In exchange for the upfront payments, energy suppliers provide discounts that CPA said have historically ranged from 8% to 12%.
CPA uses those savings to support lower and more stable electricity rates as well as customer programs, workforce development, skills training, and community energy infrastructure projects.
The latest transaction is CPA’s first prepay bond with J.P. Morgan serving as underwriter and J.P. Morgan Ventures Energy Corporation acting as the prepaid energy supplier. CPA said it also represents the first electric prepay transaction in the United States completed with J.P. Morgan.
Moody’s assigned the bonds an investment-grade Aa3 rating, while Kestrel designated them as Green Bonds.
During the initial seven-year period, CPA expects to receive approximately 1.14 million megawatt-hours of PCC1-eligible energy annually. PCC1 represents California’s highest-tier category of renewable energy.
The electricity covered by the transaction will come from existing long-term power purchase agreements representing a combined 440.8 megawatts of wind resources. CPA said the structure will help diversify its renewable energy portfolio while reducing exposure to energy market volatility.
The transaction was completed under a November 2025 authorization from CPA’s board of directors allowing the organization to execute up to $4.5 billion of new prepay transactions through June 30, 2027.
Clean Power Alliance serves 38 communities across Los Angeles and Ventura counties and provides electricity to approximately three million residents and businesses.
KEY QUOTES:
“CPA’s prepay strategy is an important tool for delivering on our commitment to provide clean, reliable and affordable energy. By building on the success of previous transactions, we’re able to secure substantial savings that reduce costs while advancing our mission to serve our communities with clean power options at competitive rates.”
Ted Bardacke, Chief Executive Officer Of Clean Power Alliance
“Reaching 8.3 billion in prepay transactions reflects the strength and scalability of this financing strategy. This latest transaction achieves long-term energy cost savings through strategic financial partnerships, helping us maintain competitive rates while supporting a diverse portfolio of renewable energy resources.”
David McNeil, C

articles.title: Children’s Hospital Los Angeles Marks $1.35 Billion Anniversary Campaign Milestone
articles.snippet:
Children’s Hospital Los Angeles has completed its Anniversary Campaign after raising a record $1.35 billion to support pediatric care, research, and education. The milestone represents the largest fundraising effort in the hospital’s 125-year history.
The post Children’s Hospital Los Angeles Marks $1.35 Billion Anniversary Campaign Milestone appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Children’s Hospital Los Angeles Marks $1.35 Billion Anniversary Campaign Milestone
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 19, 2026
Children’s Hospital Los Angeles Marks $1.35 Billion Anniversary Campaign Milestone
Children’s Hospital Los Angeles has completed its Anniversary Campaign after raising a record $1.35 billion to support pediatric care, research, and education. The milestone represents the largest fundraising effort in the hospital’s 125-year history.
CHLA announced the campaign’s completion during its 2026 gala at The Event Deck at L.A. LIVE. The event brought together philanthropists, community leaders, patients, celebrities, and other supporters while recognizing Ellen K and Kourtney and Justin Turner with the hospital’s Courage to Care Award.
The Anniversary Campaign was supported by thousands of donors, corporate partners, foundations, families, and CHLA employees. Campaign co-chairs Nikki DeLoach and Jeffrey Worthe led the effort, while Jimmy Kimmel, Sugar Ray Leonard, Chuck Lorre, and Jamie Lee Curtis served as honorary campaign chairs.
CHLA said the $1.35 billion raised will help advance pediatric medicine, accelerate scientific research, expand education initiatives, and support access to specialized care for children. The hospital is the largest provider of hospital care for children in California and operates research and education programs alongside its clinical services.
The gala also recognized Ellen K for her longstanding support of CHLA. Her involvement began after her son received emergency care at the hospital. She has since helped raise more than $4 million through KOST 103.5’s annual Giving Tuesday broadcast and has served as a longtime co-host of CHLA’s Walk & Play L.A.
Kourtney and Justin Turner were honored for more than a decade of volunteerism, fundraising, advocacy, and philanthropic support. Their work through the Justin Turner Foundation has included programs supporting children with serious illnesses and their families.
The evening also highlighted the Jackie and Gene Autry Orthopedic Center, which provides pediatric orthopedic care and includes programs focused on spine and neuromuscular disorders, hip preservation, sports medicine, and hand and upper-extremity care. The celebration concluded with a performance by Michael Bublé.
KEY QUOTES:
“As we celebrate Children’s Hospital Los Angeles’ 125th anniversary, this gala marks a defining moment in our history and an opportunity to recognize the extraordinary generosity that made the Anniversary Campaign’s success possible. Thanks to the remarkable generosity of our supporters, CHLA will continue to be at the forefront of pediatric medicine, accelerate scientific discoveries, and ensure children have access to world-class care for generations to come.”
Paul S. Viviano, President And Chief Executive Officer Of Children’s Hospital Los Angeles
“On behalf of everyone at CHLA, it is my pleasure to thank Nikki DeLoach and Jeff Worthe for so beautifully leading the Campaign. I would also like to recognize Jimmy Kimmel, Sugar Ray Leonard, Chuck Lorre, and Jamie Lee Curtis for serving as Honorary Campaign Chairs. Most importantly, it is generous individuals like all of you, who ensure CHLA will have a brilliant future for the next 125 years.”
Alexandra Carter, Senior Vice President And Chief Development Officer Of Children’s Hospital Los Angeles

articles.title: 1Komma5Grad Secures $1.35 Billion Valuation And Plans Over $112 Million Investment In Energy AI
articles.snippet:
German home electrification startup 1Komma5Grad secured a valuation of $1.35 billion in its latest financing round as the company increases investment in its energy artificial intelligence business, according to Reuters.
The post 1Komma5Grad Secures $1.35 Billion Valuation And Plans Over $112 Million Investment In Energy AI appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
1Komma5Grad Secures $1.35 Billion Valuation And Plans Over $112 Million Investment In Energy AI
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 12, 2026
1Komma5Grad Secures $1.35 Billion Valuation And Plans Over $112 Million Investment In Energy AI
German home electrification startup 1Komma5Grad secured a valuation of $1.35 billion in its latest financing round as the company increases investment in its energy artificial intelligence business, according to Reuters .
The company plans to invest more than €100 million, or approximately $112 million, in its Heartbeat energy AI platform during 2027.
1Komma5Grad describes itself as a home electrification company and is developing Heartbeat to automate a range of energy-related processes.
The platform targets functions including energy trading, billing, and metering, creating an AI-based layer to manage residential energy systems and related services.
The increased investment reflects the company’s strategy to expand beyond installing home energy systems and build software capabilities around how those assets are managed.
1Komma5Grad is also considering a significant geographic expansion.
CEO Philipp Schroeder said the company plans to expand into the United States beginning next year, citing strong investor interest as one factor behind the potential move.
The U.S. market could become an important part of the company’s next phase as it scales Heartbeat and its broader home electrification platform.
The company had previously considered a U.S. initial public offering but shelved those plans in 2025 amid uncertainty surrounding renewable energy and trade policy.
Schroeder said the company’s 2027 performance will play an important role in determining whether and when 1Komma5Grad ultimately moves ahead with a U.S. IPO.
The company has also confirmed a target of approximately $750 million in revenue for its 2026 financial year.
Hitting that target, alongside continued expansion of Heartbeat and a potential U.S. market entry, would add milestones as management evaluates the company’s longer-term capital markets strategy.
The latest financing gives 1Komma5Grad a $1.35 billion valuation while providing further support for its push to use AI to automate energy management and related processes across its platform.

articles.text:
Consonance Capital Partners Closes Oversubscribed $1.35 Billion Third Fund
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 12, 2026
Consonance Capital Partners Closes Oversubscribed $1.35 Billion Third Fund
Consonance Capital Partners closed Consonance Private Equity III with $1.35 billion in commitments, reaching the fund’s hard cap in less than four months.
The fundraising process was heavily oversubscribed, reflecting strong demand from both existing and new limited partners.
Fund III will continue Consonance Capital Partners’ strategy of investing in lower- and middle-market healthcare companies across the United States.
The fund will target businesses that can improve efficiency, reduce costs, and support high-quality patient care.
Consonance said Fund III received strong support from its existing limited partners while also adding a select group of new investors.
The investor group includes endowments and foundations, pension plans, financial institutions, and other institutional investors worldwide.
The close gives Consonance additional capital to pursue growth equity, leveraged buyout, carve-out, recapitalization, and special situation opportunities across the U.S. healthcare sector.
The firm said it remains focused on partnering with management teams building businesses that can create sustainable value across the healthcare system.
Consonance Capital Partners specializes in private healthcare investments and emphasizes companies positioned around efficiency, cost containment, and quality of care.
Support: Monument Group served as global placement agent for Fund III. Latham & Watkins LLP served as legal counsel.
KEY QUOTE:
“We are thrilled to close Fund III at its hard cap and want to thank our limited partners for their tremendous support. We also want to thank the management teams of our existing and previous portfolio companies who have been steadfast partners and major contributors to these results. We completed fundraising at a pace that reflects the confidence investors have placed in our team, strategy and results and the strength of our existing relationships. Our team remains highly focused and disciplined as we continue to partner with world-class management teams building businesses that add sustainable value to the healthcare system via a commitment to high-quality, cost-effective care.”
Managing Partners of Consonance Capital Partners

articles.title: McGraw Hill Completes $1.33 Billion Debt Refinancing
articles.snippet:
McGraw Hill completed a series of refinancing transactions involving $400 million of senior secured notes and $930 million of senior secured term loans, while also extending other debt maturities and increasing revolving credit capacity.
The post McGraw Hill Completes $1.33 Billion Debt Refinancing appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
McGraw Hill Completes $1.33 Billion Debt Refinancing
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
McGraw Hill Completes $1.33 Billion Debt Refinancing
McGraw Hill completed a series of refinancing transactions involving $400 million of senior secured notes and $930 million of senior secured term loans, while also extending other debt maturities and increasing revolving credit capacity.
The company’s McGraw-Hill Education subsidiary issued $400 million of 8% senior secured notes due 2033.
It also closed a $930 million senior secured term loan facility.
Proceeds from the transactions were used to fully redeem McGraw Hill’s outstanding 5.75% secured notes due 2028 and refinance its existing term loan facility.
The company also refinanced its senior secured cash flow revolving credit facility.
That facility’s maturity was extended to October 2031.
Available commitments were increased to $150 million, while the applicable interest rate was reduced.
McGraw Hill separately amended its asset-based revolving credit facility to extend its maturity to October 2031.
The refinancing follows a $50 million principal prepayment completed earlier in October.
McGraw Hill said the transactions extend its maturity profile and support continued reductions in gross debt.
The company remains focused on reaching a net debt-to-adjusted EBITDA leverage ratio of between 2x and 2.5x.
KEY QUOTES:
“We continue to reduce gross debt while we proactively extended our maturity wall, optimizing market conditions and recent rating agency upgrades, marking another step in our efforts to strengthen our capital structure over time.”
“These transactions offer us the ability to continue to reduce our gross debt over time, as we remain firmly committed to our net debt to Adjusted EBITDA leverage ratio target of 2.0-2.5x.”
Bob Sallmann, EVP and CFO of McGraw Hill

articles.title: Belk Secures $1.275 Billion Financing From Wells Fargo And Pathlight Capital
articles.snippet:
Belk has closed $1.275 billion in new senior secured credit facilities from Wells Fargo and Pathlight Capital, refinancing its capital structure and providing additional liquidity for working capital, inventory, and other corporate purposes.
The post Belk Secures $1.275 Billion Financing From Wells Fargo And Pathlight Capital appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Belk Secures $1.275 Billion Financing From Wells Fargo And Pathlight Capital
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 20, 2026
Belk Secures $1.275 Billion Financing From Wells Fargo And Pathlight Capital
Belk has closed $1.275 billion in new senior secured credit facilities from Wells Fargo and Pathlight Capital, refinancing its capital structure and providing additional liquidity for working capital, inventory, and other corporate purposes.
The financing consists of a $900 million asset-based revolving credit facility and a $375 million first-in, last-out term loan. Wells Fargo is serving as Administrative Agent and Collateral Agent for both facilities, while Pathlight Capital is Term Loan Managing Agent for the FILO facility.
The five-year financing replaces Belk’s existing asset-based lending, FILO, and securitization facilities. The company said the transaction simplifies its capital structure and provides increased liquidity to support seasonal inventory requirements and continued investment in its business.
Collateral supporting the facilities includes inventory, receivables, real estate, equipment, intellectual property, and Belk’s private-label credit card program.
Belk operates nearly 300 Belk, Belk Market, and Belk Outlet locations across 16 states in the Southeast and maintains an omnichannel presence through its website and mobile application. The retailer traces its history to 1888.
Pathlight specializes in private credit and asset-based loans secured by tangible and intangible assets. Wells Fargo’s Corporate and Retail Asset-Based Lending platform is expanding an existing relationship with Belk through the financing.
The transaction provides Belk with a longer-dated financing structure as it continues investing in stores, digital channels, inventory, and customer-facing initiatives.
KEY QUOTES:
“This opportunistic financing represents an important milestone and reflects the continued strength in Belk’s business by providing us with the flexibility to continue investing in our business and serving our customers. We appreciate the support, expertise and collaborative approach demonstrated by Wells Fargo, Pathlight Capital and the broader lender group throughout the transaction.”
Vince Phelan, Chief Financial Officer Of Belk
“Wells Fargo is proud to expand its relationship with Belk and deliver a flexible financing solution supporting the Company’s long-term objectives. We look forward to supporting the Company in its next phase.”
Keith Vercauteren, Division Manager And Head Of Wells Fargo’s Corporate And Retail Asset-Based Lending Platform
“We are pleased to partner with Belk and Wells Fargo on this financing. The transaction provides Belk with additional liquidity and flexibility as the Company continues to invest in its business and execute on its strategic priorities.”
Matt Williams, Managing Director At Pathlight Capital

articles.title: Michigan Students Receive 25,252 College Admission Offers And $1.274 Billion In Scholarship Opportunities Through MI College Match
articles.snippet:
Michigan students participating in MI College Match have received 25,252 college admission offers and more than $1.274 billion in scholarship opportunities through the statewide direct-admission initiative, allowing thousands of students to explore college options without completing a traditional college application.
The post Michigan Students Receive 25,252 College Admission Offers And $1.274 Billion In Scholarship Opportunities Through MI College Match appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Michigan Students Receive 25,252 College Admission Offers And $1.274 Billion In Scholarship Opportunities Through MI College Match
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 7, 2026
Michigan Students Receive 25,252 College Admission Offers And $1.274 Billion In Scholarship Opportunities Through MI College Match
Michigan students participating in MI College Match have received 25,252 college admission offers and more than $1.274 billion in scholarship opportunities through the statewide direct-admission initiative, allowing thousands of students to explore college options without completing a traditional college application.
MI College Match connects Michigan high school students with participating colleges and universities based on academic achievements, interests, preferences and other information submitted through the platform. The program opened to students on August 26, with students who completed profiles by September 21 becoming eligible for the initial round of admission offers released October 5.
Participating students have received an average of 14 college offers, while every student participating in the initial release received at least one admission offer. A total of 26 Michigan colleges and universities are participating, and the initiative is connected with more than 350 high schools through College Bound Michigan.
Each admission offer included information about either the Michigan Achievement Scholarship or the Community College Guarantee, helping students and families understand financial assistance that could make postsecondary education more affordable.
MI College Match is a partnership between Michigan College Access Network, EAB and participating Michigan higher education institutions. The initiative uses EAB’s Match technology to enable colleges to proactively identify students who may be a good fit and extend admission and scholarship opportunities directly to them.
Instead of requiring students to identify colleges, complete individual applications and then wait for admission decisions, MI College Match reverses parts of the traditional process by allowing participating institutions to approach eligible students directly.
Students create profiles containing information about their academic performance, interests, college preferences and other attributes. Participating colleges then review those profiles to determine whether to extend admission and scholarship opportunities.
The program is particularly focused on expanding college opportunities for students who may be less likely to pursue higher education, including students from low-income families, first-generation college students and students of color.
Participating institutions include Albion College, Alma College, Aquinas College, Baker College, Bay College, Calvin University, Cleary University, Davenport University, Grand Rapids Community College, Grand Valley State University, Great Lakes Christian College, Kalamazoo College, Lake Michigan College, Lawrence Technological University, Monroe County Community College, Montcalm Community College, Mott Community College, North Central Michigan College, Oakland University, Saginaw Chippewa Tribal College, Schoolcraft College, Spring Arbor University, University of Detroit Mercy, University of Michigan-Dearborn, University of Michigan-Flint and The University of Olivet.

articles.title: HPE Secures $1.2 Billion AMD Helios Order From Vultr
articles.snippet:
HPE has secured a $1.2 billion order from Vultr to deploy AMD Helios AI Rack by HPE systems across Vultr's U.S. cloud data centers. The transaction represents HPE's first order for the new AMD Helios platform.
The post HPE Secures $1.2 Billion AMD Helios Order From Vultr appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
HPE Secures $1.2 Billion AMD Helios Order From Vultr
By Amit Chowdhry
Sep 30, 2026
HPE Secures $1.2 Billion AMD Helios Order From Vultr
HPE has secured a $1.2 billion order from Vultr to deploy AMD Helios AI Rack by HPE systems across Vultr’s U.S. cloud data centers. The transaction represents HPE’s first order for the new AMD Helios platform.
The systems will be used to support growing service-provider and enterprise demand for AI model training and inference workloads.
The order extends a relationship between Vultr and Juniper Networks that began nearly three years ago and continues following HPE’s acquisition of Juniper Networks.
AMD designed Helios as a high-density platform for trillion-parameter model training and high-volume inference. Each rack integrates 72 AMD Instinct MI455X GPUs, AMD EPYC “Venice” CPUs, AMD Pensando Vulcano AI NICs and AMD ROCm software.
HPE’s networking architecture for Helios includes six HPE Juniper Networking QFX5252 scale-up Ethernet switch trays in each rack, connecting all 72 GPUs using high-bandwidth, low-latency Ethernet.
The platform combines HPE compute, Juniper networking, rack-scale engineering and direct liquid cooling to provide an integrated AI infrastructure system.
KEY QUOTES:
“AI is driving the largest infrastructure buildout in history and together with AMD and Vultr, we are building an open foundation to accelerate the next phase of AI. AMD Helios by HPE demonstrates HPE’s unique ability to engineer the complete AI architecture with rack-scale compute, scale-up networking, and direct liquid cooling, all delivered by our global services.”
Antonio Neri, President and CEO of HPE
“Demand for high-performance AI infrastructure continues to outpace available capacity, and our work with AMD and HPE enables us to bring Helios rack-scale compute and scale-up networking online for customers faster. Together, we’re delivering the memory capacity, interconnect performance, and energy efficiency customers need to run the largest and most demanding AI training and inference workloads.”
J.J. Kardwell, CEO of Vultr
